paragraphs: R. Yaakov of Kefar Gevurya, in R. Ḥaggai's time [ד׳ חגי as printed; title reading provisional]. In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of the chapter Rabbi Eliezer deMilah, [Yaakov of] Kefar Gevurya asked R. Ḥaggai. In Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 7, and parashat Ḥukkat, chapter 19; Midrash Kohelet, at 'All this I tested with wisdom'; and Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, chapter 2, halakhah 6: [Yaakov of] Kefar Gevurya ruled in Tyre that fish require ritual slaughter and that one may circumcise a gentile woman's son on Shabbat. R. Ḥaggai heard and sent him word: 'Come and be flogged.' Yaakov of Kefar Gevurya expounded in Tyre: 'To You silence is praise'—the remedy for everything is silence. A pearl that has no price: everyone who praises it diminishes it, Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter HaRo'eh. He expounded concerning those appointed for money: 'Woe to him who says to wood: Awake!' Jerusalem Talmud, end of the last chapter of Bikkurim. He is buried there in Nevartayin, at the crossroads (גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]). See R. Elazar HaModa'i.
